items.title: Finding the Measures of the Sides of a Rectangle

sections.normalized_html: The perimeter of the rectangle [MATH: PQRS] below equals [MATH: 25\, \mathrm{cm}.] What is the length of [MATH: \overline{PQ}?]
sections.readable_text:
The perimeter of the rectangle [MATH: PQRS] below equals [MATH: 25\, \mathrm{cm}.] What is the length of [MATH: \overline{PQ}?]

[IMG: /graphics/50e16746e371910fac024a6da095bcc0]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The opposite sides of a rectangle are congruent, so we have

[MATH: PS=QR=5\, \mathrm{cm}.]

For the same reason, we also have

[MATH: PQ = RS.]

Now, since the perimeter is [MATH: p=25 \, \text{cm},] we have

[MATH: p|= PQ + RS + PS + QR; 25|= PQ + PQ + 5 + 5; 25|= 2PQ + 10; 15|= 2PQ; 7.5|= PQ.]

Therefore, [MATH: PQ = 7.5 \, \text{cm}.]
